reproduces: R1 wrong-configuration (runs/2026-09-12-q42-review/results.json): an emit whose Plugins are the request's reversed was accepted
note: Every rejection below is reached END TO END through the CLI (plan -> run) with a fake-probe behaviour, never by calling the Validator directly. The mutation is applied to EVERY emit-writing probe of the arm, so the arm is internally consistent: a mutation on one probe alone is caught by the within-arm rule that already exists and would prove nothing about D2.

plan.schemaVersionRule: A-1: SCHEMA_VERSION 1 -> 2, so a plan without `requested` is refused by name rather than silently certified
plan.armsRequestedRule: D1: plan.arms[].requested = {plugins: [{name, sha256|null, path|null, hashSource}], overlays, providers, population, states}

candidate-02-unstated.why: D1: a name the scope does not list is hashSource `unstated`, sha256 null. The fixture scope lists only the four base-order plugins, so PatchA.esp is the unstated one. D2(c) then accepts the emit's own hash for it and records an entry under validation.identityLimits.

plan.providersRule: D1: plan.configuration additionally keeps the scope's providers

healthy.why: The controls. A contract that rejects wrong identities is worth nothing if it also rejects right ones.

identityLimitsOn.rule: D2(c): a request plugin with hashSource unstated is accepted with the emit's own hash recorded and listed under validation.identityLimits

differentPopulations.rule: D2(g)/(h): two supported probes declaring different populations over the same plugins carry different fingerprints and both pass; content is compared to the request, fingerprints only within one population/state

consumed.rule: D3: the consumed block of a child that states no identity is the ARM's requested, configurationSource `plan`, fingerprint null with a fingerprintNote; the baseline arm's block is the scope's configuration verbatim (configurationSource `scope`, the scope's fingerprint)

candidate-01-reorder.why: never the scope's baseline fingerprint copied onto another arm

rejections.damage: every emit of arm candidate-01-reorder carries the request's plugins REVERSED (masters last), Source still correct, Fingerprint recomputed over the reversed list so only the order rule can fire
detailContains: the same names in a different order
rejections.rule: D2(b): the emit's plugin names in order must equal the request's names in order; the detail names the first differing position with the expected and the found name, and says whether the set differs or only the order
rejections.rulingApplied: A-2: positions count from 1 and the detail reads `plugin order differs from the request at position N: expected X, found Y` then `; the same names in a different order` when only the order differs. The request is [Skyrim.esm, Update.esm, FixtureTarget.esp, FixtureBase.esp] and the emit is that reversed, so the first differing position is 1: expected Skyrim.esm, found FixtureBase.esp, same names.

rejections.damage: every emit of arm candidate-01-reorder consumes FixtureTarget.esp at a sha256 one nibble away from the scope's, Fingerprint recomputed so only the hash rule can fire
rejections.rule: D2(c): every request plugin with a stated sha256 must be consumed at that sha256 (detail: plugin, both hashes, 12 hex)

rejections.damage: every emit of arm candidate-01-reorder carries Fingerprint ffff...ff (64 f) with the plugins, providers, overlays, population and state otherwise correct
rejections.rule: D2(e): the emit's Fingerprint must equal the canonical digest of its own Plugins / Providers / Overlays / Population / State. A mismatch: `the fingerprint is not the digest of the stated configuration`

rejections.damage: every emit of arm candidate-01-reorder carries a Configuration whose Plugins list is empty (Fingerprint recomputed over the empty list, so the emit is self-consistent)
rejections.rule: D2(a): identity-missing when there is no Configuration, OR an empty Plugins list, OR any plugin lacking a name or a 64-hex sha256. An incomplete identity is never accepted, first receipt or not.

rejections.damage: the reverse part of arm candidate-01-reorder (emit stem candidate-01-reorder.reverse, run on the BASELINE order) emits the CANDIDATE's plugin order instead
detailContains: the same names in a different order
rejections.rulingApplied: A-2: the reverse part's reference is the BASELINE's request [Skyrim.esm, Update.esm, FixtureBase.esp, FixtureTarget.esp]; the emit carries the candidate's order, so the first differing position is 3: expected FixtureBase.esp, found FixtureTarget.esp, same names.
rejections.rule: D2: the reference for part `reverse` is the BASELINE arm's requested (the reverse run is the probe on the baseline order with the candidate as --base); the reverse part is validated against that reference, never exempted
rejections.healthyControlInSameCase: in every other scenario of this case the reverse emit carries the BASELINE order and is accepted — the reverse part is not simply always rejected
